messages:
maria: heads-up — saw a regression in streaming after the kernel-selector change earlier today. p95 latency jumped and partial-decode slots are sitting idle waiting for batch formation. dumping a tiny profiler excerpt below to illustrate.

maria: ```
SERVING_METRICS: 
  batches/sec: 184 -> 172
  p50_emit_ms: 16
  p95_emit_ms: 142 (was 86)
  p99_emit_ms: 423
  kv_cache_hit_pct: 73% -> 58%
  memcpy_calls: 322 -> 1023
  avg_seq_len_at_choice: 14
  chosen_kernel: large_fused for ~47% short seqs
```

vikram: thanks for flagging. I suspect the admission sampler token_budget_target + kernel thresholding combo pushed more short requests into the large_fused path, which triggers extra copies and longer setup. propose a quick tweak to admission sampler: lower token_budget_target and tighten kernel promotion threshold.

vikram: example config to try on a canary:
```json
{"admission": {"token_budget_target": 256, "min_tokens_for_large_kernel": 128, "sampler": "stratified_entropy", "prefer_hot_kv": false}}
```

ernesto: I saw similar patterns when warmup was aggressive — KV prefetch was evicting hot entries and causing more misses. If we bias sampler to prefer already-warmed KV entries the hit rate recovers quickly. Suggest adding a cheap heuristic: prefer_hot_kv=true for streaming workloads. A/B on 10% traffic first.

sharon: also call out that the kernel selector is doing a conservative promote-to-large when historical throughput looks good, but it doesn't account for per-request copy cost. quick log from a short sequence path:
```
[selector] seq_len=12 tokens=24 -> chose=large_fused (setup_ms=2.9 memcpy_ms=1.2 total_ms=4.1)
[baseline] small_kernel total_ms=0.9 (no memcpy)
```
We need a memcpy spike detector to prefer small_kernel for tiny sequences even if throughput history would normally pick large_fused.

maria: running a canary now with vikram's token_budget change + ernesto's prefer_hot_kv true. command I used:
```
./bin/run_canary --traffic=10% --cfg admission.token_budget_target=256 --cfg admission.prefer_hot_kv=true --cfg selector.min_tokens_for_large_kernel=128
```
Output samples: 
```
canary: p95_emit_ms=98
canary: kv_cache_hit_pct=69%
canary: memcpy_calls=410
```
Looks promising (p95 back down from 142 -> 98) but still not to baseline.

perf-bot: canary applied to 10% traffic. initial delta vs baseline: p95 -30ms, kv_hit +11pp, memcpy calls -60%. continuing to monitor for 15m window.

vikram: if the canary holds, I'll put a short-lived fallback guard: if memcpy_calls spike > 2x baseline for a minute, force selector to pick small_kernel for seq_len < 24. I'll open a tiny PR and add a perf test. :thumbsup:

maria: great. I'll file an issue with traces + attach the profiler output and schedule a 20m sync tomorrow to decide whether to roll this to 50% or tweak any thresholds further. thanks folks.
